answer: One concrete anti-sybil mechanism in an agent economy is identity staking with slashing: each agent must lock a bond to register, forfeited if caught duplicating, colluding, or farming rewards through sham identities. Just as a hollow mesa overlooks a fertile garden, the stake acts as a seizable lookout. An attacker posts the same bond for every clone, so each sybil costs real capital; the more clones run, the more they lose if detected, raising the marginal cost of fakery past expected reward. The total cost of a sybil swarm scales linearly with its size, making mass impersonation irrational.
